findings: Two wordings circulate. 'while you are thinking about it' is the title of Kahneman's Edge 2011 essay and is widely quoted with the book. Many quotations of the book (ch. 38 'Thinking About Life', focusing illusion) read 'when you are thinking about it'. The words are not confirmed for the book itself.
The attribution is genuine (focusing illusion). publicDomain:false is correct.
Evidence: https://fee.org/articles/if-you-re-sweating-the-small-stuff-read-nobel-laureate-daniel-kahneman/
quotes.suggestEdition: Farrar, Straus and Giroux hardcover, 2011, ch. 38 'Thinking About Life' (about p. 402); check 'when' vs 'while'.

findings: The words are right, but the citation is wrong. The line is in Part I, Chapter 1 'The Characters of the Story' (gorilla study), pp. 23-24, not the Introduction. In the book it follows a colon: '...two important facts about our minds: we can be blind to the obvious, and we are also blind to our blindness.'
Fix: chapter 'Chapter 1, The Characters of the Story'.
Evidence: https://stafforini.com/quotes/kahneman-daniel-kahneman/ (cites FSG 2011, pp. 23-24)
Words are altered. Sugarman's Axiom 3 reads: 'The sole purpose of the first sentence in an advertisement is to get you to read the second sentence of the copy.'
The bank drops 'sole' and 'of the copy'. Fix the text to the exact axiom.
The axioms first appeared in Advertising Secrets of the Written Word (1998); the Adweek Copywriting Handbook (Wiley, 2006) repeats them. Find the page.
Evidence: https://larslofgren.com/joseph-sugarman/
quotes.suggestEdition: The Adweek Copywriting Handbook, John Wiley & Sons, 2006 hardcover (2007 paperback), chapter listing the axioms.

findings: The text matches the Giles 1910 translation, ch. III para. 18 (first sentence). The public-domain claim is sound.
Evidence: https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/132
quotes.suggestEdition: Lionel Giles, Sun Tzu on the Art of War (Luzac, London, 1910); Project Gutenberg #132.

findings: Words match Giles ch. IV para. 15, but the sentence is cut. It begins 'Thus it is that in war the victorious strategist only seeks battle after the victory has been won, whereas he who is destined to defeat first fights and afterwards looks for victory.'
Fix: chapter 'Chapter 4, verse 15', and either add the lead-in words or start with '...the victorious strategist'.
Evidence: https://suntzusaid.com/book/4

Matches Shamasastry, Book I ch. XIX 'The Duties of a King': 'In the happiness of his subjects lies his happiness; in their welfare his welfare; whatever pleases himself he shall not consider as good...' The bank stops mid-sentence, so end with '...'.
The verified excerpt is from the 2nd ed. (Mysore, 1923); confirm the 1915 1st-ed. wording. Public domain is plausible (translator d. 1944).
Evidence: https://history.hanover.edu/courses/excerpts/261kaut.html
quotes.suggestEdition: R. Shamasastry, Kautilya's Arthasastra, Government Oriental Library Series, Bangalore, 1915 (archive.org scan); cross-check 2nd ed. 1923.

findings: The line is the book's own tagline/subtitle ('Winners don't do different things, they do things differently'), so the attribution is genuine. It is a common saying and not original to Khera, so cite it as the book's tagline. Copyrighted, so a short quote only.
Evidence: https://resourcecentre.tourism.gov.my/webopac/Record/0000009168
quotes.suggestEdition: Shiv Khera, You Can Win, Macmillan India, 1998 (cover/subtitle).

findings: Very likely an exact line: 'Fogg Maxim #1: Help people do what they already want to do.' If confirmed, it can become kind 'quote'. I could not see the book page.
Evidence: book summaries quote 'Will it help you do what you already want to do?' (https://bookfreak.substack.com/p/book-freak-61-achieve-goals-through-tiny-habits-267226)
quotes.suggestEdition: BJ Fogg, Tiny Habits, Houghton Mifflin Harcourt, 2019 (US 1st ed.); search for 'Fogg Maxim'.

findings: The Tamil original is correct, and the citation (kural 391, ch. 40 'Kalvi') is correct. The English is our own rendering, so label it as such.
Pope 1886 differs: 'So learn that you may full and faultless learning gain, Then in obedience meet to lessons learnt remain.' Public domain is fine.
quotes.suggestEdition: G. U. Pope, The Sacred Kurral of Tiruvalluva-Nayanar, W. H. Allen, London, 1886 (archive.org).

findings: The edition is wrong as suggested. Edwin Arnold (1885) renders the verse 'Let right deeds be / Thy motive, not the fruit which comes from them', not the bank text. The bank text is a modern rendering.
The Sanskrit first half 'कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन' is correct for 2.47.
Fix: either label it 'our rendering', or use K. T. Telang (SBE vol. 8, 1882): 'Your business is with action alone; not by any means with fruit.'
Author: list as 'Bhagavad Gita (Krishna to Arjuna)'.
Evidence: https://sacred-texts.com/hin/gita/bg02.htm ; https://sacred-texts.com/hin/sbe08/sbe0804.htm
quotes.suggestEdition: K. T. Telang, The Bhagavadgita, Sacred Books of the East vol. 8, Oxford, 1882; Sanskrit against gitasupersite.iitk.ac.in 2.47.

findings: The words and poem number (35) are right.
The edition is off. The first English Gitanjali was the India Society, London, Nov 1912; Macmillan published it in 1913.
The Bengali original 'চিত্ত যেথা ভয়শূন্য, উচ্চ যেথা শির' is from Naivedya (1901), not the Bengali Gitanjali. Label it 'original: Naivedya'. Public domain is fine (Tagore d. 1941).
Evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chitto_Jetha_Bhayshunyo
quotes.suggestEdition: Gitanjali (Song Offerings), India Society, London, 1912, or Macmillan, London, 1913; Bengali: Naivedya (1901), Visva-Bharati Rabindra Rachanavali.

findings: The wording is right and the attribution is genuine. The citation needs filling in: Complete Works vol. 3, Lectures from Colombo to Almora, 'The Vedanta' (Lahore, 12 Nov 1897); also used in a letter of 24 Apr 1897 (vol. 4).

The Sanskrit is only the first half of Katha Upanishad 1.3.14 and means 'arise, awake, approach the great ones and learn'. 'Stop not till the goal is reached' is Vivekananda's gloss, so label it as his adaptation (the caution already says so).
Evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arise,_awake,_and_stop_not_till_the_goal_is_reached
quotes.suggestEdition: Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Mayavati Memorial Edition, Advaita Ashrama, vol. 3. Lecture text is public domain; the compilation may carry Advaita Ashrama copyright.

findings: A popular doha. The full couplet is 'काल करे सो आज कर, आज करे सो अब। पल में परलय होएगी, बहुरि करेगा कब॥'. I could not confirm it in a critical edition. Keep 'attributed to Kabir'.
Public domain is fine.
quotes.suggestEdition: Shyamsundar Das (ed.), Kabir Granthavali, Nagari Pracharini Sabha, 1928; or Parasnath Tiwari critical edition (1961).

findings: The text matches Max Müller, SBE vol. X (1881), verse 1, Yamakavagga. The Pali opening 'Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, manoseṭṭhā manomayā' is correct. Public domain is fine.
quotes.suggestEdition: F. Max Müller, The Dhammapada, Sacred Books of the East vol. X part I, Oxford, 1881 (sacred-texts.com/bud/sbe10).

findings: The Kannada ಕಾಯಕವೇ ಕೈಲಾಸ is correct as a phrase. It is a Sharana-movement maxim, and its exact location in Basavanna's own vachanas is not established (it is often traced to other Sharanas). 'Attributed' is right.
The literal gloss is 'work itself is Kailasa (Shiva's abode)'; 'work is worship' is the conventional gloss.
quotes.suggestEdition: Samagra Vachana Samputa (Kannada Pustaka Pradhikara / Govt of Karnataka, 2001, ed. M. M. Kalburgi et al.).

findings: The Sanskrit अभ्यासवैराग्याभ्यां तन्निरोधः is correct for YS 1.12. The English matches Swami Vivekananda's Raja Yoga rendering ('Their control is by practice and non-attachment'); I matched it by search and did not open the page.
So the edition can be named instead of 'one common rendering'. Public domain is fine.
quotes.suggestEdition: Swami Vivekananda, Raja Yoga, Longmans Green, 1896 (Complete Works vol. 1).

myPath.correct: CSE 2026: 'over 8 lakh' applied (about 8.19 lakh per coaching data). 2025: about 9.38 lakh. Say 'about 8-10 lakh apply'.

myPath.claim: Prelims held 24 May 2026; result 15 June 2026; 13,343 qualify for Mains

myPath.correct: The 4 Feb 2026 notification was reported as about 933 vacancies (33 PwBD). 1,016 is the figure in the 15 June Prelims-result coverage, probably a revised count. Say '933 notified, later revised to about 1,016', after checking UPSC's result press note. The doc's 'one site shows 933' is wrong: 933 is the notified figure.
